newsitem.title: USA: New Brunswick 630 MW nuke seen down for three wks.
newsitem.headline: New Brunswick 630 MW nuke seen down for three wks.

text.p: New Brunswick Power Corp's 630 megawatt Point Lepreau nuclear power plant is expected to be shut for at least three weeks while the company repairs a leaking heavy water pipe, a company spokesman said.
The unit, at Lepreau, New Brunswick, northwest of the Maine-New Brunswick border, was shut January 16 due to the leak in an outlet feeder pipe, company spokesman Roland Krause said.
"We are anticipating a shutdown in the order of three weeks," Krause said Wednesday.

New Brunswick Power has been purchasing spot power to make up for electricity lost by the outage, the spokesman said, adding the average cost of replacement power is expected to be about C$450,000 (US $333,000) a day.
Replacement power costs are higher than average, the spokesman said, adding "with the cold weather and higher load in New Brunswick, alternate generation sources are limited."
New Brunswick Power normally exports electricity into Maine and New England.
Up until about four years ago, New Brunswick Power exported an average of 230 megawatts into the U.S. Northeast under long-term contracts, the spokesman said.
Many of those contracts have expired however, and recent exports to the U.S. have averaged much lower levels, he said.
New Brunswick Power directly and indirectly services about 340,000 electricity customers, and the Point Lepreau plant makes up about 30 percent of the utility's generation, Krause said.
